limitation: These are two final bounded real-provider trials, with two earlier two-trial rounds preserved including a failed end-to-end attempt. They demonstrate these exact synthetic inputs, not a latency or reliability benchmark. Retention/revocation concurrency coverage is separately owned by the Session backend PostgreSQL suite.
lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action
verification_basis: Same original two objectives and canonical summary, using the original outer transaction/SAVEPOINT pattern that exposed the v2 persistence failure. No fixture timestamp adjustment, response replay, or manually admitted internal screenshot flag was used. Both provider calls and both canonical result writes completed on final sources.
source_freeze_confirmation: Session backend owner confirmed the clock-fix source freeze with 87/87 affected tests, including real PostgreSQL Session 42/42 and provider 34/34, plus typecheck. Migration 055 and 056 checksums remained unchanged. The probe separately verified both applied database checksums and all recorded source hashes remained stable.

resolved_observations.final_observation: Both final replies ask for the missing date/time zone or suggest checking the existing capture. Neither asks to upload/share the screenshot again.
Neither final reply asserts shared participants, agreement, or reviewing together.

resolved_observations.finding: Task expiry exceeds transaction-clock created_at plus 30 days
resolved_observations.final_observation: The final bound case preserved the same delayed Session creation inside an outer transaction. Its requested expiry was 2026-10-06T20:04:04.688Z; PostgreSQL clamped the stored expiry to 2026-10-06T20:04:01.647Z, exactly task created_at plus 30 days. Persistence completed. The 3.041-second shortening retains the fixed deadline; it never extends source or Session retention.
